Situation1: There is a scheduled family gathering on the calendar.
Situation2: They occasionally give casual advice when asked about minor career choices.
Story: I glanced at the calendar, a bright circle around Saturday reminding me of the family gathering. My daughter had called twice this week, excited for everyone to be together, and my grandson had already asked if I’d bring my famous lemon bars. I could almost hear the laughter and see the kids running around the backyard. But as I was setting out the ingredients, my phone buzzed—a message from Maya, the young woman I’d been mentoring at work. She sounded anxious, asking if I had time to talk about a job offer she’d just received. She rarely reached out, and I knew how much this decision meant to her. I felt the weight of both worlds pressing in: the warmth and expectation of my family, the trust and need in Maya’s voice. My heart tugged in two directions, guilt and responsibility swirling together. I wanted to be present for my family, to soak in every moment, but I also knew how much a few words from me could mean to Maya right now. I stood in the kitchen, phone in hand, torn between the two calls on my time and care.
